_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel's four-week climb finally broke — EIA's week-ending-8/10 read has the national average down 9c to $5.257/gal as Strait of Hormuz talks cooled the risk premium. That's the first drop since early July, so ease off the surcharge push and requote fuel off today's number, not last month's high. Spot's leaning the same soft direction — DAT's dry van, reefer, and flatbed rates all cooled again this week — and Southeast reefer out of Atlanta/Miami keeps easing as GA/FL produce season winds down, so don't chase last month's board on reefer; ask what's posted today before you counter.

_sourcing.status: Diesel TURNED this cycle: first decline after four straight weekly increases — $5.257/gal for week ending 2026-08-10, down 9c from the confirmed $5.348 (week ending 8/3), on Strait of Hormuz talks easing the risk premium. Corroborated across three independent outlets. asOf advanced to 2026-08-10 on diesel's account and trend flipped from 'up' to 'down'. Spot/modality/lanes/commodityRates remain carried-forward for an EIGHTH straight cycle — searches this week again surfaced a real softening story (dry van/flatbed/reefer all cooling per DAT/FTR trade press) but the exact figures keep splitting across linehaul-vs-all-in and week-vs-month bases, so nothing numeric was promoted. See refreshBlockers for egress status.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE, confirmed 2026-08-18 (searched): $5.257/gal for the week ending 2026-08-10, down 9c from the prior confirmed week's $5.348 — the FIRST decline after four consecutive weekly increases. Corroborated across THREE independent outlets, all EIA/USDA-sourced with consistent figures: (1) IndexBox 'EIA Weekly Fuel Price Report: Gasoline and Diesel Prices as of August 10, 2026' — national average $5.257, regional breakdown (California $6.618, West Coast $6.033, Central Atlantic $5.535, East Coast $5.193, Midwest $5.181, Gulf Coast $5.044, Lower Atlantic $5.034); (2) FleetOwner 'Diesel prices fall as Strait of Hormuz talks ease crude oil market concerns' — EIA data released 8/11, down 9c to $5.257, East Coast biggest mover (-11c to $5.193), West Coast -10c to $6.033, Gulf Coast -10c to $5.044, Midwest -8c to $5.181, still +$1.503 YoY; (3) HaulerMath/USDA AgTransport (independent EIA-weekly aggregator) also shows $5.257 for week ending 8/10. All three agree on the figure, direction, and driver (Hormuz de-escalation talks, not resolution). Ruled out a false-positive: a search summary surfaced '$3.713/gal, down 4c' framed as an 8/18 EIA release, but that figure and its regional breakdown (Gulf $3.340, Midwest $3.702, West Coast $4.455, East Coast $3.733) are wildly inconsistent with the current $5+ price regime and match no credible current source — almost certainly a stale/mismatched-year search artifact (same failure pattern as last cycle's stale June headline); correctly excluded, not promoted. Checked specifically for a week-ending-8/17 release (today, 8/18, is EIA's normal Tuesday publish day) — WebSearch confirms no such data was surfaced/available yet at refresh time (IndexBox's most recent post is still the 8/10 week), so $5.257/wk-ending-8/10 is the freshest CONFIRMED number, not a guess at today's release. No primary eia.gov fetch was possible (still blocked, see refreshBlockers) — this is 3-source secondary corroboration, consistent with the bar cleared each of the last five cycles.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: carried-forward from the app's Q2 2026 snapshot ($3.83/mi). Not verified this cycle — DAT/SONAR WebFetch still blocked, and WebSearch again produced mutually contradictory 'current' figures: DAT's own July Dry Van Report cites van CONTRACT rate at $2.39/mi linehaul (+13c) or $3.01/mi including fuel surcharge (+12c from June), while a separate mid-August SPOT summary (same search session) cites dry van spot at $2.93-2.95/mi with no fuel-inclusion label stated consistently across repeated queries of the same underlying data point — contract vs. spot, linehaul vs. all-in, and monthly vs. weekly bases all mixing in the search synthesis. Not promoted; the reconciliation problem is unchanged from prior cycles.
_sourcing.modality: carried-forward from the app's Q2 2026 modality ranges. Not verified this cycle. Real signal found (DAT/FTR trade press, week of Aug 9-15, 2026): dry van spot ~$2.93/mi (down 2c w/w, described elsewhere as 'largest weekly drop since at least 2008' for linehaul), reefer ~$3.38/mi (essentially flat, gains fell short of seasonal expectations), flatbed ~$3.54/mi (down 6-7c w/w) — directionally these ARE softening/cooling per FleetOwner ('Truckload spot rates fall as dry van, flatbed, and reefer markets underperform') and TheTrucker ('DAT: Demand for trucks softens, ending van and reefer spot rate run'). But whether these are linehaul-only or fuel-inclusive kept flipping between identical-looking search summaries of the same week — not clean enough to overwrite the current ranges without a primary DAT Trendlines read. None promoted.
_sourcing.commodityRates: carried-forward, unchanged. Not verified this cycle. See lanes note below on why Fresh Produce specifically was not marked down despite the reefer-easing story — no clean $/mi replacement figure found, only percentage-off-peak and per-load commentary.
_sourcing.lanes: carried-forward, unchanged, for a THIRD straight cycle despite trying again to find a specific-lane replacement number. DAT's own Reefer Produce Report headlines this cycle ('Yakima is the only market moving up right now,' 'Florida's done. Yakima's tightening. California just reset.') confirm the seasonal handoff continuing, and a June-dated snippet had Atlanta reefer at '$1,000-$1,200 per load (-8%), lowest in 2026 tracking' and Yakima corridor lanes (LA +5%, Miami +4%, Atlanta +3%) — but these are per-load not per-mile, several weeks stale, and don't cleanly convert to the file's $/mi or $/load Yakima format for the current week. No fresh Atlanta-Miami or Yakima-Northeast $/mi figure found this cycle either. Flagging again: if DAT Trendlines becomes fetchable, both lanes are the first candidates to reprice down given three straight cycles of directional confirmation.
_sourcing.blurb: rewritten this cycle: diesel's four-week climb broke, coaching flipped from 'push the surcharge harder' to 'ease off / requote fuel off today's lower number' per the standing rule. Kept the Southeast reefer caution (now a third cycle of directional confirmation) and added a line noting spot (dry van/reefer/flatbed) is also trending soft per trade press, without putting an unreconciled number in the blurb.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: Eighth straight cycle without clean spot/modality/lanes corroboration, though the DIRECTION (softening) is now well-corroborated across many outlets this cycle specifically for spot equipment rates and reefer lanes. Do not promote numerics until dat.com/trendlines or eia.gov's own tables are actually reachable — the linehaul-vs-all-in / spot-vs-contract mismatch has been the persistent blocker, not a lack of trade-press coverage.

refreshBlockers: Re-tested egress first, as instructed: curl to https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/ returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' again today (also re-tested the EIA xls data endpoint and www.dat.com — both same 403); WebFetch tool also failed EGRESS_BLOCKED on www.eia.gov, www.ttnews.com, www.fleetowner.com, www.thetrucker.com, and even a control domain (www.wikipedia.org) — confirming WebFetch itself is broadly blocked this session, not just freight/energy sites specifically. The agent-proxy status endpoint logged fresh connect_rejected entries for www.eia.gov:443 and www.dat.com:443 at refresh time ('gateway answered 403 to CONNECT'). Block is unchanged across all eight weekly refreshes from 07-07 through 08-18 — destination-side 403 via the agent proxy, not a transient proxy outage. WebSearch works and this cycle it delivered a genuinely new, clean result: diesel's four-week climb broke, now confirmed down to $5.257/gal for the week ending 2026-08-10 (three-outlet corroboration, see dieselPerGal note) — promoted to LIVE, asOf advanced to 2026-08-10, trend flipped up→down. Checked for a fresher week-ending-8/17 release (today is EIA's normal publish day) and found none yet surfaced. Spot/modality searches again produced mutually contradictory 'current' figures split across linehaul-only vs. all-in vs. contract bases and different reference weeks (see per-field notes) — not promoted, though the softening DIRECTION is now well-corroborated. Lanes: tried again per this cycle's brief to replace the Atlanta-Miami/Yakima entries, found only stale per-load (not per-mile) figures from June — not clean enough to promote. Broader web-fetch access (not just search) to a primary source like eia.gov or dat.com/trendlines would let spot/modality/lanes get the same clean-primary-source treatment diesel has now gotten five cycles running, instead of waiting on secondary-outlet search summaries that keep splitting on methodology (linehaul vs. all-in vs. contract, weekly vs. monthly).
